* Pass the native build settings to pnpm 12 from .mjs pnpmfiles

pnpm 12 loads only JavaScript pnpmfiles (.js, .mjs, .cjs): it fails on
.pnpmfile.mts with ERR_PNPM_PNPMFILE_NOT_FOUND. It also runs the
pnpmfile in a separate Node.js process, so the npm_config_* variables
that the pnpmfiles set on process.env never reached the install scripts.

Each native install root (the workspace, build, remote) now has a
.pnpmfile.mjs that exports createNativeBuildHooks() from
nativeBuildEnv.ts, so the code stays in TypeScript. Its updateConfig
hook returns the variables as extraEnv, which pnpm passes to every
dependency install script and lifecycle script. extraEnv can't remove a
variable, so a native build key that the root's .npmrc doesn't set gets
an empty value; node-gyp treats it like a missing one. The three files
are added to .eslint-allowed-javascript-files.

pnpm passes neither --frozen-lockfile nor its command line to the
pnpmfile or to scripts, only the command: `pnpm ci` and its aliases are
reported as npm_command `ci`. The root hook then sets
pnpm_config_frozen_lockfile for the installs of the separate install
roots. A local `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` can't be passed on, so
preLaunch.ts and update-all-grammars.ts also set
PNPM_CONFIG_FROZEN_LOCKFILE. In CI, pnpm's default freezes every install.

References to .pnpmfile.mts (install state hash, CI cache keys, change
detection, ripple, dependencies-check) now name .pnpmfile.mjs.

* Pin pnpm 12.16.0 and adapt the conversion tooling and settings to pnpm 12

12.16.0 is the first pnpm 12 release with the fixes for a wrong peer
variant under the hoisted linker (pnpm/pnpm#17395) and for re-importing
patched packages on every install (pnpm/pnpm#17188).

Settings of every install root:
- pmOnFail: ignore. With a pinned packageManager, pnpm 12 records the
  pnpm packages of every platform in a second YAML document of
  pnpm-lock.yaml, which js-yaml's load, yaml.parse and GitHub's
  dependency graph can't read; a frozen install fails without it. ignore
  keeps the lockfiles single-document. pnpm then no longer switches
  another version to the pinned one; the preinstall's check names it.
- skills.dirs: []. pnpm 12 links the agent skills that approved
  dependencies ship into the skill folders of the coding agent it
  detects (.github/skills or .agents/skills here), and asks for
  approval on every install.
The setting names are checked against the pnpm 12.16.0 documentation.

Lockfiles: pnpm records pnpmfileChecksum for a pnpmfile with hooks. The
conversion generates lockfiles in a copy without the pnpmfile, so it
adds the checksum (SHA-256 of the pnpmfile with LF line endings, as
pnpm computes it) where pnpm writes it, and validates the result with
--ignore-pnpmfile. verify-locks checks the checksum (k) and fails on a
second YAML document (l).

getPnpmCommand also runs Corepack's native pnpm-native executable
directly, so nested installs started by `corepack pnpm` reuse it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pnpm 12's hoisted linker links a dependency to the same version in

* Engineering - move the native build targets from .npmrc to package.json

The `.npmrc` files of the root, `build` and `remote` only held node-gyp and
prebuild-install settings (`target`, `runtime`, `disturl`, `ms_build_id`,
`build_from_source`, `force_process_config`). pnpm ignores them there and npm 11
warns about them, so move them to a typed `nativeBuild` field in each install
root's `package.json` (see `NativeBuildConfig` in
build/npm/pnpm/nativeBuildEnv.ts) and delete the three `.npmrc` files.

- The `.pnpmfile.mjs` hooks pass the field as `npm_config_*` variables, with
  the same values as before. `forceProcessConfig` replaces the
  `forceProcessConfigOnDarwin` hook option (still macOS-only); the pnpmfile
  checksums in the lockfiles change accordingly.
- `getElectronVersion()` and the new `getServerNodeVersion()` in build/lib are
  the typed readers of the Electron and server Node.js versions; the
  preinstall, gulpfile.reh, darwin signing, useRunnerNodeForServer, the test

  dependencies ship into the skill folders of the coding agent it
  detects (.github/skills or .agents/skills here), and asks for

conversion generates lockfiles in a copy without the pnpmfile, so it

--ignore-pnpmfile. verify-locks checks the checksum (k) and fails on a
second YAML document (l).

directly, so nested installs started by `corepack pnpm` reuse it.

Replace the raw-specifier @typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports check
with a small local rule, local/code-no-restricted-path-imports, which
resolves each import (relative or vs/ alias) to a repository path before
matching it against restricted globs. This catches dynamic imports,
import() types and non-canonical relative specifiers, and no longer
matches vs/sessions or unrelated folders named 'sessions'. The exact
four-file allowlist (#346756) is unchanged.

and only checks require() when it is the unbound global. Document that
computed dynamic imports are not enforced.

Absolute filesystem specifiers were treated as node modules, so an
